label: sec:non-comm-probability-q-clt-intro
html:
In the sense of Voiculescu and Biane [biane1998], the inductive-limit Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_\infty(q) equipped with the Jones–Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M (z = q^3/(q^2+1)) forms a non-commutative probability space. Because \mathrm{tr}_M vanishes on the three-row antisymmetriser ideal and factors through the positive-definite Temperley–Lieb quotient \mathrm{TL}_\infty(q), the Gelfand–Naimark–Segal (GNS) completion yields a finite von Neumann algebra in which the braid generators \sigma_i act as non-commuting random variables and their joint moments evaluate link invariants.

This section establishes three foundational theorems of the non-commutative probability sector:

  1. The algebraic GNS embedding and non-commutative probability dictionary: Proving positivity of the centered Hecke variance at z = q^3/(q^2+1) on \mathrm{TL}_n(q) without threshold restrictions on q > 1, and translating operator-algebraic invariants into physical observables.
  2. The q-deformed Central Limit Theorem and macroscopic washout: Demonstrating how non-commuting microscopic braid generators converge in the macroscopic A \to \infty limit to continuous q-Gaussian distributions over the Plancherel measure \mathbb{M}_{n,q}.
  3. Exponential brane-tower decay and Causal Fermion Systems (CFS) comparison: Bounding the \hbar_q^{2n} brane-tower tail via q-Laplacian spectral decay and comparing the categorical state space with Finster's Causal Fermion Systems framework.
